questions.prompt: A block reduction uses shared memory down to 32 values. Why finish with shuffles?
options: Only one warp is left: shuffles need no shared memory and no block-wide barriers
questions.explanation: Lanes of a warp exchange registers directly.

questions.prompt: Exclusive scan of [4, 0, 3, 1, 2]: what is the last element?
Why does a single-pass scan take tile ids from an atomic counter?
options: So a tile only waits on tiles that have already started; blockIdx order isn't guaranteed
Atomics are required for float sums
questions.explanation: Forward progress requires waiting only on started tiles.

questions.prompt: A privatised shared-memory histogram is slow on a mostly-black image. Why?
options: Lanes collide on the same shared counter, so atomics serialise
questions.explanation: Skew moves contention into shared memory.

questions.prompt: Which provide a legitimate grid-wide synchronisation point?
questions.explanation: __syncthreads is per block; a fence orders but doesn't wait.

questions.prompt: What makes compaction via exclusive scan stable, unlike atomicAdd slot reservation?
options: Each kept element's position is the count of kept elements before it, so order is preserved
